budgets.note: Do not auto-merge an upstream refresh whose lightweight artifact peak exceeds the hard limit. Peaks above the preferred target but within the limit are reviewable; peaks above the limit block the merge and must file an actionable Runtime Lab task.

correctness.note: Focused coding-agent correctness gate run after every upstream refresh: the offline representative task plus the pytest subset below. No live credentials required.
correctness.representative_task: q1-small-edit (FOO_LIMIT search + edit 10->20 + build/test, same workload as the coding-qualify and lite contracts)

deltas.obsolete_when: Upstream removes the pruned subsystems itself (no TUI/web/serve command table in src/index.ts, no Question/WebSearch/LSP/plan imports in tool/registry.ts, lazy bootstrap.ts). Then the coding-only entrypoint adds no compile-graph delta and the patch can be dropped.
deltas.purpose: Exclude TUI/web/serve/MCP/LSP/formatter/share/snapshot-watcher subsystems from the coding-only compile graph while the full build keeps working.

deltas.obsolete_when: Upstream bounds Task-tool subagent transcript injection itself (tool/task.ts routes renderOutput through Truncate with tail direction + retrieval hint) and routes remaining tool results through Truncate. Then the fork bound is upstream behavior and the patch can be dropped.
deltas.purpose: Bound Task-tool subagent transcript injection and remaining tool results through the existing Truncate service (tail direction + file-backed retrieval) so one verbose subagent cannot grow parent-session memory without a bound.
deltas.validator: automation/opencode_bounds.py:retention_points + fork regression tests in the patch doc (Change 3)

deltas.obsolete_when: Upstream removes the in-process HTTP hop itself (cli/cmd/run.ts no longer dispatches via Server.Default().app.fetch, no TCP/mDNS listen on the run path). Then the direct runner adds no plumbing delta and the patch can be dropped.
deltas.purpose: Bypass in-process HTTP/server/SDK plumbing on the headless run path (direct session/agent/provider/tool dispatch) while provider semantics stay unchanged.

invariants: Full build (packages/opencode/src/index.ts + packages/opencode/script/build.ts + scripts.build) stays usable; every delta is additive or scripts-only except the bounded-output in-place bound.
No custom direct provider/API client: all model access stays through the existing provider/session/agent loop.
Tracking stays in kodmial/runtime-lab; the fork carries no separate product backlog.

memory_smoke.budget_gate: evaluate_sync_budget: peak above the 512 MiB hard limit blocks the merge; peak above the 450 MiB target is reviewable but never silently merged as an improvement.
memory_smoke.method: python3 automation/memory_benchmark.py hermetic probes (--version peak tree + startup walls) plus Docker --memory=512m --memory-swap=512m real-agent trials where available; same telemetry vocabulary as automation/opencode_qualification.py, no second measurement stack.
memory_smoke.note: Offline CI runs the hermetic probe; resourced builders run the full real-agent trial against the same harness.

rebuild.note: CI rebuilds the lightweight artifacts after every upstream refresh with the upstream-supported Bun compile path; a missing or checksum-mismatched artifact fails readiness and never falls back to the pinned baseline binary.

refresh_failure.note: Any refresh failure (rebase conflict, rebuild failure, correctness failure, smoke over budget, obsolete-delta ambiguity) files an actionable Runtime Lab task via render_refresh_failure_task() instead of silently leaving the deployed fork stale. The task records fork SHA, upstream candidate SHA, failed stage, evidence, and the next retry step.
refresh_failure.title_template: P1: OpenCode fork refresh blocked at <stage> (fork <fork-sha12> vs upstream <upstream-sha12>)
